Fix mdns publishing service to stop growing json cache

- `pgrep` could not see the `avahi-publish` processes so it was constantly thinking they had not been started and thus kept adding to the cached JSON.
- Used `avahi-resolve` instead to check if a domain had been published rather than trying to get a list of published domains.

files, it wasn't explicitly clear how the game is being initialized on
page load. Usually, the game initialization logic would be placed in a
separate script file that is referenced in your HTML, or directly in a
script tag within the HTML itself. However, this isn't present in the
provided index.html.

Given your index.html and game.js, I'm assuming the Game class is being
automatically initialized upon import of the game.js file. As I
suggested earlier, one approach is to create a new initGame function in
your game.js file which initializes the game:

```javascript
// game.js

// ... existing code ...

export function initGame() {
    if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
        window.game = new Game(true);
    }
}
```

And then in your index.html, add a script to call this function when the
window is loaded:

```html
<!-- index.html -->

<!-- ... existing code ... -->

<script type="module">
import { initGame } from './game.js';

window.onload = function() {
    initGame();
};
</script>
```

Now, the game will be initialized when the window loads, and not just
when game.js is imported. You should update your tests to reflect this
new initialization logic.

Again, I apologize for any confusion. I hope this clears things up, but

ChatGPT
GitHub Actions is a tool that enables you to automate, customize, and
execute your software development workflows right in your GitHub
repository.

You're seeing an error message because your repository doesn't have a
package-lock.json file. The package-lock.json file is automatically
generated when npm install is run and it describes the exact tree that
was generated such that subsequent installs are able to generate
identical trees, regardless of intermediate dependency updates.

Here are a few ways to resolve this:

Add a package-lock.json file:
Run npm install in your project's root directory locally. This will
create a package-lock.json file if there isn't one already.
Commit and push the package-lock.json file to your GitHub repository.
Use npm ci instead of npm install:
If you're using npm install in your GitHub Actions workflow, you may
want to switch to npm ci. npm ci is a more reliable and faster
alternative for continuous integration environments. However, it
requires a package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json file to be present.
Here's a basic example of a GitHub Actions workflow file for running npm
test:

```yaml
name: Node.js CI

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [14.x]

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
      uses: actions/setup-node@v2
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
    - run: npm ci
    - run: npm test
```

Remember that you still need to commit and push your package-lock.json
or npm-shrinkwrap.json file to your GitHub repository to use npm ci.

Disable the package-lock.json check:
If you don't want to use a package-lock.json file, you can disable the
check in your .npmrc file by adding the following line:

```npm
package-lock=false
```

Please note that by doing this, you lose the benefits of having a
package-lock.json file. Also, make sure to update your GitHub Actions
workflow to use npm install instead of npm ci, because npm ci requires a
package-lock.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json file to work.

### Eval description
Evaluates a models ability to determine the size of an obscured grid
using information only from initial constraints and a visible viewport.

### What makes this a useful eval?

Requires the model to go beyond simple instruction following to solve a
task that requires pattern recognition and interpretation.


<details>
  <summary>"GPT4 Pattern Recognition"</summary>


> The AI could benefit from better pattern recognition in problems like
this, to understand how the relationship between parts of a system (like
a viewport and a larger grid) can reveal information about the whole
system.
https://chat.openai.com/share/4aeb8ed6-6dff-4f26-a946-aefe8c2fa511


I provided the prompt (submitted in this eval) to ChatGPT and tried to
get it to reword the prompt by telling it that I didn't understand it.

<details>
  <summary>(original) prompt for reference</summary>


`Given a viewport into a larger grid, calculate the total number of
cells in the grid. The grid consists of cells, each labeled with an
index. The labeling starts at 1 in the first cell located in the top
left corner of the grid and increments by 1 with each step. The final
cell in the bottom right corner of the grid is the size of the grid. The
viewport shows only a small portion of the (square) grid. Provide the
answer directly, or the mathematical representation e.g (rows * cols)`
</details>

GPT-4 proceeded to misinterpret the task (which I expected), but when I
challenged it's assumptions with the original facts provided it realized
that my original instructions were sufficient and the prompt didn't
require any changing.
> The original instructions you provided were quite clear in retrospect.
The misunderstanding was on my part for not correctly identifying the
pattern from the viewport. The instructions were providing all necessary
information for someone to identify the grid size by observing the
numerical pattern in the viewport.


</details>
